question: When different native taxa are observed on the same source-calendar days, are their daily GPS night/day movement positions ranked differently and are their astronomical-daylength slopes recurrent across distinct source studies?

source_DOI_frame.astronomical_reference: Goose original study common reference daylength (not the same latitude as other studies)

recorded_biology: Original q=night-minus-day log1p GPS straight-line displacement velocity, not actual minutes of activity. Native q/photoperiod are original source-calendar studies, not the full-study annual native sample.
rank_requirement: A native pair has a resolved relative q position only if ORIGINAL source original-tagged bootstrap nominal interval is entirely positive or negative. Retain unresolved native pair effects as unresolved; no favorable sign selection.
photoperiod_heterogeneity: Native study-reference q~daylength slopes are interpreted by ORIGINAL source tagged animal bootstrap nominal signs; both positive and negative within same DOI define exploratory opposite-signed native trends. This is not a directly causal daylength treatment, and reference daylength cannot be compared in numeric magnitude across latitudes.
independent_replication: For the SAME repeated native pair (mule deer minus bighorn), compare all three fixed original GPS schedules in two different DOI source studies. Original q-rank direction in both is source-level observational repeatability; the positive versus negative native daylength slope contrast is supported only in Wyoming and unresolved in Utah, selected after prior Wyoming outcome.
month_sensitivity: Report earlier Illinois and Wyoming year×month conditional native pair outcomes with source-month cluster bootstrap and goose 5-block within-month outcomes, distinct from all-month source-native tagged regression effects. Utah month conditional was not run, so NOT_EVALUATED, not zero.
inference_unit: One independently published original field study DOI is a replication unit. Three IL native taxa, two WY, two UT, three geese are ten study×native pairs but only FOUR original source studies and EIGHT unique registered taxon labels. Some populations or source study recruitment may still be correlated.
source_support: Preserve exact original source numbers of shared calendar days 169,193,199,120 and number of year×month blocks 9,8,10,5. No original calendar event dates, individual IDs, GPS position or exact source data released.
history: Do not change previous original 48-source signed shortwave directional external nonreplication or old 12 ERA5 raw JSON source version HOLDS. This is photoperiod and GPS velocity observational calendar comparison only.
publication_limit: Post-outcome source-conditioned exploratory pattern; study/date and location relative photoperiod can covary with habitat, season, GPS duty cycle, species distribution, migration route and resource availability. No causal climate or global community assembly mechanism.
